title: How foodservice equipment dealers manage product data
summary: Foodservice equipment dealers pull manufacturer data from AutoQuotes, KCL, Specifi and the FEDA Data Portal into ERP and quoting, then enrich it for ecommerce.
body_markdown:
Foodservice equipment dealers manage product data by pulling manufacturer content from shared industry sources (AutoQuotes, KCL, Specifi, and the FEDA Data Portal) into their quoting tool and ERP, then reshaping it for their own website and catalog. The hard part is the last step: the data arrives built for quoting and CAD layouts, so dealers still have to normalize utility specs, dimensions, and certifications into structured fields before ecommerce filters, freight, and search work.


## Where foodservice equipment dealer product data comes from


Most FES dealers don't type product records from scratch. The data comes from four overlapping sources, each built for a different job.


**AutoQuotes (AQ).** The quoting database many dealers already work in. AutoQuotes says its CPQ carries[over a hundred data fields for each of nearly 1 million SKUs from more than 800 manufacturers](https://autoquotes-fes.com/aq-cpq/) , covering descriptions, pricing, spec sheets, warranty, and CAD/Revit content, maintained by a content team. Dealer ERPs plug into it directly: Business Central partners describe AQ products[flowing into the ERP during quote and order processing](https://syssolutionsllc.com/industries/foodservice-equipment-cloud-erp/) , and Advantive lists[support for the AQ products API](https://www.advantive.com/industry/distribution/foodservice-equipment-supply-software/) for converting quotes to orders.


**KCL.** The design-side library. KCL hosts manufacturers'[2D and 3D DWG files, RFA (Revit/BIM) files built to FCSI USA BIM or IFSE BIM standards, spec sheets, photos, and manuals](https://kclcad.com/manufacturer/) , and links out to ENERGY STAR certification and the CFESA service locator.


**Specifi.** Another specification platform, with a manufacturer-side[catalog for configuring and downloading DWG/Revit files and spec sheets, an asset organiser, and an API for automating updates](https://us.specifiglobal.com/products/) .


**FEDA Data Portal.** The distributor association's own repository. FEDA describes it as[an editable database of product information from FES manufacturers, with uniform data standards for each attribute](https://www.feda.com/about-the-feda-data-portal-and-support-center) . Manufacturers load data by CSV, align it with a[Data Mapping Tool, and follow a published Product Glossary](https://learn.feda.com/data-portal-manufacturer-information) . When FEDA announced the repository in 2021, it said manufacturers could[submit data and dealers could access it at no cost](https://www.fermag.com/articles/feda-creates-product-data-repository/) , and its[DP+Q Partners program is building the connections to dealer ERP systems and a new CPQ that works with the portal](https://www.feda.com/news/new-tech-options-energize-a-future-vision-for-industry) .


On top of these, some dealers use an ecommerce-oriented catalog service. Beedash, for example, describes its Corestack product as giving restaurant equipment dealers[a repository of 300,000+ products optimized for online listing](https://beedash.com/what-is-product-information-management-pim/) , with trade-discount pricing and change alerts.


The upshot: a dealer's product record is usually stitched from a quoting feed, a PDF spec sheet, and a CAD file, and none of those was designed to drive a faceted web catalog.


## Which attributes actually matter for FES products


A walk-in cooler and a countertop fryer share almost nothing, but the fields that decide whether an item can be installed are consistent. The FCSI/NAFEM spec sheet guidelines are a good map of what manufacturers are asked to publish. They recommend sheets show[connected load in voltage, phase, amps, and watts; cord set type by NEMA configuration; kW and amps per line; gas type and BTU per hour; water and waste connection sizes; exhaust CFM; refrigerant type, charge, and capacity; and minimum door entry clearances](https://www.fcsi.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/Spec-Sheet_guidelines_revised-2015.pdf) , plus agency symbols such as UL, NSF, and CSA.


For a dealer catalog, that collapses into three groups:


- **Utilities:**` voltage` ,` phase` ,` amperage` ,` kw` ,` nema_plug` (for example` 5-15P` or` 6-50P` ),` gas_type` (natural or LP),` btu_per_hour` ,` water_inlet_size` ,` drain_size` .
- **Fit:**` width` ,` depth` ,` height` ,` crated_weight` ,` door_entry_clearance` ,` side_clearance` for combustible surfaces.
- **Compliance:** NSF listing, UL or CSA listing, ENERGY STAR status.


Certifications deserve their own fields, not a line in the description. NSF food equipment standards are product-specific:[NSF/ANSI 4 covers commercial cooking, rethermalization, and hot food holding; NSF/ANSI 7 covers commercial refrigerators and freezers; NSF/ANSI 12 covers ice makers](https://www.fda.gov/media/133482/download) . ENERGY STAR only applies to certain categories, including[refrigerators and freezers, ice makers, dishwashers, ovens, griddles, fryers, steam cookers, hot food holding cabinets, coffee brewers, and electric cooktops](https://www.energystar.gov/products/commercial_food_service_equipment) . A filter called "ENERGY STAR" on a mixer category is a sign the field is being populated from marketing copy rather than the source. Confirm current listings against the certifier's own directory before publishing.


For a full field-by-field list by equipment type, see our[foodservice equipment attributes reference](https://www.anglera.com/blog/foodservice-equipment-attributes) .


## Where dealer ecommerce product data breaks


Quoting databases are tuned for a salesperson who already knows the model number. Ecommerce is tuned for a buyer who filters. That gap produces predictable failures.


**Utilities trapped in text.** "208/240V 1PH 30A NEMA 6-30P" lives inside a description string, so the` voltage` filter is empty. One industry vendor notes that the same measurement shows up as[36 inches, 36″, and 36in, and that core attributes like voltage are frequently missing](https://beedash.com/the-spec-sheet-wasnt-built-for-this-and-its-showing/) , which breaks exact-match filters.


**Variants collapsed or exploded.** One fryer model sold in natural gas and LP, or a combi oven at 208V and 480V three-phase, needs to be either one parent with variant axes or separate SKUs with clear differentiators. ERP setups that[track variants on equipment like voltage, pressure, and fuel type](https://syssolutionsllc.com/industries/foodservice-equipment-cloud-erp/) help, but only if the attribute values feeding them are clean.


**Options and accessories with no relationships.** FCSI guidance asks manufacturers to[list all options and accessories on the sheet and note required options](https://www.fcsi.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/Spec-Sheet_guidelines_revised-2015.pdf) . On a dealer site those often arrive as prose, so a casters kit or a required gas connector never shows up as a linked add-on.


**Freight and install fields blank.**` crated_weight` , carton count, and door entry clearance decide LTL quotes and whether the unit fits through the back door. They usually sit in the spec sheet PDF and often never make it into the web record.


**Stale prices and specs.** Manufacturers revise sheets and price books on their own calendars. A dealer that imported once and never re-synced shows last year's model with this year's price.


## How a dealer catalog gets enriched, step by step


The practical workflow looks like this:


1. **Start from what you already have.** Export the active SKU list from the ERP or AQ, with manufacturer, model, and any existing fields.
2. **Attach the source documents.** Match each SKU to its current spec sheet, KCL or Specifi asset, and manufacturer product page.
3. **Extract into a fixed schema.** Pull utilities, dimensions, clearances, and certifications into typed fields with controlled units (` in` ,` lb` ,` BTU/hr` ), not free text.
4. **Reconcile conflicts.** When the AQ record says 120V and the current spec sheet says 208V, flag it for a person to resolve instead of picking one silently.
5. **Publish and keep watching.** Push to the PIM, ERP, or ecommerce platform, then re-check when manufacturers publish new sheets.


For illustration, a dealer with 15,000 web-listed SKUs and 25 target fields has 375,000 values to verify. At an assumed 30 seconds per value for a person reading PDFs, that is about 3,125 hours, which is why many catalogs stay partly filled.


This is the point where "who does the work" becomes the real question. A PIM stores and distributes the record; see our[guide to PIM software](https://www.anglera.com/best/pim-software) if you are choosing one. It does not read a Vulcan or True spec sheet and fill` btu_per_hour` . Anglera sits between the sources and whatever system you already run: it extracts values from the actual spec sheets, manufacturer sites, and ERP fields, scores each one, and flags conflicts for review rather than inventing values. Your PIM stores the data; Anglera does the work. It can start from a flat CSV or ERP export, typical implementation is 30 days or less, and you can read[how Anglera works](https://www.anglera.com/how-it-works) step by step.


## How to decide what your dealership needs


Use your channel mix to pick the depth:


- **Mostly quoted project work:** AQ plus KCL or Specifi often covers it. Enrichment matters for freight and install fields, not filters.
- **Growing ecommerce or a smallwares-plus-equipment site:** You need structured utilities, dimensions, and certifications on every listed SKU. A catalog service gives you breadth; enrichment gives you filterable depth.
- **Multiple systems (ERP, PIM, web, marketplaces):** Decide which system holds the master record, then feed it clean attributes. Adding another data source without a schema just adds another version of the truth.


For a broader overview of categories and buying considerations, see our[foodservice equipment guide](https://www.anglera.com/blog/foodservice-equipment-guide) .


## Keeping the record current


Treat enrichment as ongoing practice rather than a one-time import. Manufacturer data moves, new attributes get requested (a marketplace wants` nema_plug` as its own field next quarter), and new SKUs keep arriving. Anglera runs that as a maintained, source-grounded process for[foodservice equipment and supply distributors](https://www.anglera.com/solutions/foodservice-equipment-supply-distributors) , backfilling a new attribute across the catalog from the source documents and keeping it in sync with the PIM, ERP, or flat file you already use.
